subject: history_social
passage: Since the 1990s, Welsh has been a required subject in schools across Wales, and in many areas pupils are taught largely through Welsh. Sociolinguist Carys Llywelyn surveyed residents of a town in Gwynedd, a county in northwest Wales where the language is widely spoken. She argues that the schools have been very successful at teaching young people to speak Welsh but have done much less to make it a language used at home, and that the gap between the two is clearest among the town's youngest residents.

data.title: Welsh Speaking and Home Use by Age in a Gwynedd Town

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support Llywelyn's argument?

choices.A: Daily home use of Welsh was higher among 5- to 15-year-olds than among any older age group in the town.
choices.B: Residents aged 65 and older were the most likely of any age group to speak Welsh daily at home.
choices.C: Among 5- to 15-year-olds, 82% could speak Welsh but only 31% used it daily at home, the widest gap of any age group.
choices.D: The 5- to 15-year-olds had a higher share of residents able to speak Welsh than any other age group surveyed in the town.

explanation.why: Llywelyn's argument is about the gap between being able to speak Welsh and using it at home, and she says that gap is widest for the youngest group. The choice must give both figures for the youngest group and compare its gap with the others. The gap is 51 points for ages 5 to 15, compared with 33, 22, 19, and 17 points for the older groups.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Only 31% of 5- to 15-year-olds used Welsh daily at home, the second-lowest share; the 30–49, 50–64, and 65+ groups were all higher.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is true (47%), but it describes home use among the oldest residents rather than the gap among the youngest.
explanation.C: Correct. The youngest group shows a 51-point gap between ability and home use, wider than any other group's gap.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This shows the schools' success in teaching Welsh, but it leaves out home use, so it says nothing about the gap.
